newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Common Fund finances Kenya, Tanzania sisal project.
newsitem.headline: Common Fund finances Kenya, Tanzania sisal project.

text.p: The Common Fund for Commodities, a U.N. affiliate, said on Monday it had granted finance for the development of the sisal crop in Tanzania and Kenya -- aiming to improve cultivation and processing practices.

The fund said it would donate $2.57 million to the five-year project and provide a further $1.25 million as a soft loan. The balance of the $5.375 million costs would be covered by other international institutions and the Belgian government, it added.
"Successful orientation of the sisal sector through the implementation of the project will have a substantial impact on the national economies of the beneficiary countries," it said.
The project also aims to develop new varieties of sisal -- a crop which generates fibre used to make twine -- as well as train manpower in various aspects of production and marketing.
"It is estimated that a mere rehabilitation of the sisal industry to its original level of production in Kenya and Tanzania will raise employment by over 250,000," the fund said.

Outside the direct beneficiaries, the results of the project will be passed on to other sisal producting countries -- Brazil, China, Philippines, Haiti, Venezuela, Cuba, Angola, Mozambique Ethiopia and Morocco.
